uncited: *   **Inputs:** A set of unposed or posed input images of a scene; a reference style image; camera parameters (intrinsics and extrinsics) for the input images.
*   **3D Feature Grid:** An explicit 3D voxel grid storing high-level feature vectors instead of implicit density/color values at coordinates.
Let the grid dimensions be $D_x \times D_y \times D_z$.
Each voxel stores a feature vector $\mathbf{f} \in \mathbb{R}^C$.
*   **Ray Sampling:** Standard NeRF ray sampling is used to query points along rays.
Points are sampled along the ray, and their corresponding 3D coordinates are used to trilinearly interpolate features from the 3D Feature Grid.
**Scene Representation Construction:** Construct a 3D scene representation using a grid of deep features.

*   **Volume-Adaptive Normalization:** Instead of computing mean and variance from the sampled batch of points (which varies per ray and view), the method learns the mean and variance of the *whole volume*.
*   **Channel-wise Self-Attention:** Apply channel-wise self-attention to transform each 3D point independently.
**Deferred Style Transformation (DST):** Transforming every sampled 3D point is memory-intensive because NeRF queries hundreds of points per pixel.
DST defers the style transformation to 2D feature maps.
*   Render the scene to obtain 2D feature maps (or intermediate features) from the camera view.
*   Apply the style transformation to these 2D feature maps.
**Optimization:** The network is optimized to minimize the difference between the rendered stylized images and the target style, while preserving the geometric structure of the original scene.
In StyleRF, the feature transformation is applied to the features $\mathbf{f}_i$ associated with each sample point $i$.
